title: Understanding Fold and All-In in Texas Hold'em
summaryJa: ポーカーの基本用語である「フォルド」と「オールイン」について説明します。フォルドは現在のハンドを降りることで、オールインは所持チップをすべて賭けることです。
segments: Texas Hold'em is a popular poker game. Players try to win money by making the best hand.
But winning is not just about good cards. You need to understand important words.
Two key words are "fold" and "all-in". Learning these words helps you play better.
The word "fold" means to stop playing in the current hand. When you fold, you give up your chance to win the pot.
The pot is all the money players have put into the game. You fold when your cards are not good.
Or you fold because you think another player has better cards. For example, you have weak cards.
Another player bets a lot of money. You think you cannot win.
So you fold. Your cards go to the middle of the table.
You lose the money you already put in. But you save money because you do not bet more.
"All-in" is different from fold. All-in means you put all your remaining chips into the pot.
You use this word when you have very few chips left. Or you think your hand is very strong.
For example, you have ten chips. You bet all ten chips.
Now you cannot bet anymore in this hand. You are all-in.
Other players can still bet. But you can only win the money that was in the pot when you went all-in.
Fold and all-in are opposite actions. Fold means you stop playing and save chips.
All-in means you risk all your chips for a big win. New players should practice these words and actions.
Understanding when to fold and when to go all-in is important for success at the poker table.
